summary: The main article describes a visible-light-promoted C3-carbamoylation of 2H-indazoles, featuring 1 optimization table, 1 general scheme, 3 scope schemes, and 4 mechanistic/application schemes. The study includes late-stage modification of drugs and peptides and evaluates antitumor activity.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Representative drugs and bioactive molecules containing 2H-indazole scaffold.
items.description: Displays chemical structures of pharmaceutical compounds like Niraparib, Pazopanib, and S-217622 which incorporate the 2H-indazole core.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions a .
items.description: A screening of photocatalysts, bases, and solvents to determine the optimal conditions for the carbamoylation of 2-phenyl-2H-indazole.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Visible light-promoted transition metal-free direct C3-carbamoylation of 2 H -Indazoles.
items.description: General reaction scheme showing the coupling of 2H-indazoles with oxamic acids using 4CzIPN and visible light.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scope of 2 H -indazoles.
items.description: Exploration of various substituted 2-aryl-2H-indazoles and their yields in the carbamoylation reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Scope of oxamic acids.
items.description: Demonstrates the compatibility of different oxamic acids, including alkyl, aryl, and secondary amine derivatives.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Late-stage modi fi cation of drugs and peptides.
items.description: Shows the application of the method for modifying complex molecules like Nateglinide, Gemfibrozil, and various peptides.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Radical scavenge experiment.
items.description: Mechanistic study using TEMPO to confirm the involvement of radical intermediates in the reaction pathway.

items.heading: Scheme 6
items.caption: Stern-Volmer luminescence-quenching experiments and oxidative potential.
items.description: Fluorescence quenching data and electrochemical potentials used to support the proposed photoredox mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 7
items.caption: Proposed mechanism.
items.description: Detailed step-by-step catalytic cycle involving SET, decarboxylation, and radical addition to the indazole ring.

items.heading: Scheme 8
items.caption: In vitro antitumor activity of compound 4d.
items.description: Biological evaluation showing the IC50 values of a synthesized derivative against Ramos cancer cells compared to 5-FU.
